summary: Iteration 202: tested the sign-up email domain check, the password or confirm-code step before changing a sign-in method, and the renewal receipt. Backend: 20/20 pytest tests passed, and the node esim_renewal suite printed PASS with receiptSaved:true. Frontend: the /cloudivr/signup email tab and the landing eSIM checkout Account step both show the typo, throwaway and can't-deliver messages. Alice's add-phone flow works: Send is disabled until a password is entered, a wrong password shows 'That password isn’t right.', and the right password plus a code changes the phone. The phone-only account flow works: confirm code to the current phone, then the add-email form (gmial rejected), then a code, and the email is added. On a phone account, changing the phone also asks for a confirm code first.

minor.issue: A request with no password still counts toward the 5-try lockout (confirmed: 5 calls with no password lead to a 429 on the 6th call, which had the right password). The UI disables Send until a password is entered, so this mainly affects API clients.

The takenBy check (409 phone_taken/email_taken) and the email domain check run before confirmed(), so a signed-in session can find out whether a phone or email belongs to another account without the password or a confirm code. Consider calling confirmed() first.
The confirmToken is not single-use: it can be reused for 10 minutes for any number of phone/email start calls. Acceptable, but it could be consumed after a successful verify.

design_issues.screen: Settings → Sign-in methods (account with no password)
issues: In the Confirm step, Cancel sits on its own line under 'Send me a code', while the add form shows its buttons side by side. The confirm token is also not shared between the Email and Phone rows, so a user who adds an email and then changes the phone must confirm again.

action_items: Optional: do not count requests with no password toward the acct-confirm lockout
Optional: call confirmed() before the takenBy checks to prevent account enumeration
critical_code_review_comments: email-check.js: a DNS timeout or SERVFAIL returns true (fail-open), which is intended. A null MX ('.') falls back to the A record, so domains that say 'no mail' (RFC 7505) still pass. Minor.
email-check.js: the example.com/org/net bypass only applies when WEB_CLOUDIVR_DRY_RUN=true. That is correct.

spenza.js receipt(): sends only when the account has an email. It includes line, amount, date, active-until, wallet balance and reference. The reference is the line id (d._id), not the wallet transaction id, so consider using the txn id. receipts[] is capped at 24 entries, and emailed is set using arrayFilters on 'at'. Fine.
The checkout QR email field (esim-co-qr-email) is not domain-checked; only the account email is. Probably out of scope.
seed_data_creation: Created throwaway accounts named TEST_iter202 (test_iter202_*@example.com, test.iter202.*@gmail.com/outlook.com, which were deleted, and random +1555 phone-only accounts). Alice's phone changed from +15555243109 to a new +1555 number during the UI test, and her acct-confirm attempt counter was cleared.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Base API is /api/cloudivr-web. To clear sign-up and code limits, delete the webLoginAttempts keys reg|*, phone-send|<ip> and acct-confirm|<chatId>. After a phone sign-up, the onboarding modal (onboarding-skip) blocks Settings clicks. Alice has a password; do the lockout test only on throwaway accounts.
